header:
Date: 2025-10-28
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (EmberRise - ML Infra), Carmen Diaz (EmberRise - Platform), Samir Patel (EmberRise - Security), Tina Park (EmberRise - SRE)
Shared: artifact-delivery-checklist.pdf (Redwood), quant-kernel-notes.pdf (Redwood)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: all right folks thanks for joining, we wanted to walk through the artifact delivery flow and then dig into batching and quantization tradeoffs for the on-prem pilot. audio is a bit clipped on my side, apologies if i repeat.
[00:22] Jordan: no worries, we have Carmen and Samir on the line, Jordan here. main ask is: how do we get bundles into our air-gapped cluster and avoid driver mismatches.
[00:35] Priya: good question. high-level flow: we produce a signed artifact bundle (tar.gz) with sha256 and a gpg signature, plus a separate driver bundle matching the kernel. for air-gap we recommend the courier USB + tamper-evident seal or encrypted shipper. the bundle contains: model.pt, compiled kernels, kv-cache-warmup snapshots (optional), and a license blob.
[00:58] Carmen: quick Q — the license blob, is that hardware-locked? we need to know for our procurement.
[01:08] Alex: yes it's an offline license with hw fingerprinting. activation happens via an offline exchange, customer provides a fingerprint generated by our activation tool, we return an activation token that the on-prem node can consume without outbound connectivity. there is also an HSM path if you need key material to stay on-prem.
[01:28] Samir: and audit logs? we need to capture activation events and download checksums in our SIEM.
[01:35] Priya: we emit signed audit events in the bundle install step; they can be forwarded to your logging stack. will attach schema in follow-up.
[01:45] Tina: driver compatibility — we run a mixture of A100s and a couple of older R5300s, worried about CUDA/CuDNN mismatch.
[01:58] Priya: yep—recommend matching the driver package to the runtime we compiled against. we ship a driver shim and libcompat layer; however older cards may need fallback kernels that sometimes cost ~5-12% perf. we should capture exact driver versions on your nodes.
[02:15] Jordan: noted. can you give an example of perf impact for kv cache warmup vs cold start? our SLO is p95 <= 120ms for short chats (~64 tokens).
[02:29] Priya: warm KV cache is huge — if you warm prefix keys (we provide warmup snapshots), you can get p95 down to ~40-60ms on a single A100 for typical 64-token flows. cold cache will be higher, maybe 180-250ms depending on model and batch. batching also changes the equation — micro-batching helps throughput but increases tail latency.
[02:56] Alex: to add — we have continuous batching with a latency ceiling; you can set batching window to 5-20ms for lower tail, or larger windows for throughput.
[03:10] Carmen: what's the recommended batch size and window for 100 qps target?
[03:17] Priya: depends on model sequence length. for 2k context models we saw optimal throughput at batch sizes 8-16 with window 10ms, but if your median is short (<=128 tokens) you can push batch 32 with 15ms window. we'll produce a tuning table.
[03:36] Jordan: and quant — int8 vs int4, any gotchas?
[03:40] Priya: int8 is mature; usually minimal quality drop for many tasks if calibrated. int4 gains more cost savings but may need per-layer fine-tune or calibration sets. we recommend running eval prompts you care about; we'll provide a small eval harness. also note some kernels need special quantized matmul paths and may require specific GPU firmware/drivers.
[04:03] Samir: are there any model variants that you recommend for on-prem when customers want deterministic hashes for audit?
[04:10] Alex: we can provide a pinned model artifact (immutable checksum) and also reproduce compiler flags. that helps compliance.
[04:18] Tina: about KV caching — is it per-instance or shared across cluster? when we scale replicas, do they share prefix cache?
[04:27] Priya: currently per-replica, but we have an optional shared prefix cache service for Dedicated deployments — in air-gapped mode it's possible but requires setting up the internal cache service and configuring network policies. for now pilot can use per-replica warmup snapshots.
[04:46] Jordan: how do we validate the bundle on arrival? checksum and gpg verify, but would you recommend running a smoke benchmark before enabling service?
[04:55] Alex: yes run a smoke script we include: verifies checksums, validates driver modules, runs a short perf harness to check cold start and warm start latencies. we'll share the smoke-run output schema.
[05:12] Carmen: there was a note in your docs about "kv warmup snapshot size can be large" — how big are we talking?
[05:19] Priya: depends on prefix distribution. typical snapshots for conversational workloads can be 50-200MB per model variant. we can compress and dedupe before packaging.
[05:30] Samir: PCIe topology concerns — will we need MIG slicing or is full GPU recommended?
[05:36] Priya: full GPU gives best latency. MIG is possible if your GPUs support it; some quant kernels run slower on MIG slices. we can test on your hardware.
[05:48] Alex: quick interjection — Carmen, you mentioned earlier the air-gap courier window?
[05:52] Carmen: yes, we have a quarterly approved courier list. we can schedule the USB transfer in week of Nov 10, pending SOW.
[06:02] Alex: great — we'll align timelines.
[06:05] Priya: diving back into batching: when we looked at similar customers, tuning the batching window had more impact on p99 than batch size. p95 is usually manageable with small windows but p99 needs either narrower window or fallback to small-batch hot paths.
[06:23] Jordan: fallback meaning automatic route to smaller model or single-token path?
[06:28] Priya: yes, automatic fallback to a lower-latency variant or enabling fast-path kernels that trade off slightly higher token cost. we can configure at route level.
[06:36] Samir: from security perspective, we need to vet the driver bundle — are drivers signed and reproducible?
[06:42] Alex: drivers we include are the vendor-supplied binaries plus our shim. we provide checksums and a reproducible build log for the shim; final signing happens before shipping. you can verify signatures with our public key.
[06:55] Tina: what about OS-level dependencies? our images are RHEL 8.8 with a custom kernel.
[07:02] Priya: we'll provide a compatibility matrix. sometimes custom kernels require rebuilding kernel modules; our packaging includes kernel module source if needed. that's why we ask for exact uname -r outputs ahead of time.
[07:17] Jordan: can we talk numbers — throughput per A100 for your 2.7B variant at batch 16? rough QPS.
[07:24] Priya: for 2.7B with int8 we saw ~150-220 QPS per A100 for short tokens at batch 16; int4 can go higher but depends on accuracy tolerance. we'll run a bench on your exact model.
[07:41] Alex: note those numbers assume a warm cache; cold cache is substantially lower. include warmup in pilot to get realistic numbers.
[07:50] Carmen: on the license activation flow, can you walk us through the offline exchange? step by step?
[07:55] Alex: sure. step 1: customer runs the offline fingerprint tool, which collects HW IDs and signs them with a local key. step 2: deliver the fingerprint to Redwood via secure courier or our portal (if allowed). step 3: Redwood generates a signed license token tied to the fingerprint and returns it to customer on transport. step 4: customer applies token; runtime validates signature and unlocks the runtime. all events are logged.
[08:27] Samir: is there an option for time-limited trial tokens?
[08:30] Alex: yes, we can issue short-lived trial tokens for pilots. trial mode notes will be in the checklist.
[08:38] Priya: back to perf — we should discuss KV shard sizing. if you have many concurrent sessions, shard count affects hot-key contention. recommend starting with N = number of GPUs * 2 and tune from there.
[08:56] Jordan: okay noted.
[09:00] [09:00] Tina: question on monitoring — what's in the bundle for consoleless observability?
[09:06] Alex: we include a local telemetry agent that aggregates token-level latency histograms and cost estimates. in air-gapped mode it writes to local storage; you can configure forwarding to Splunk/ELK.
[09:18] Carmen: will that agent require outbound HTTPS by default? we can't allow that.
[09:22] Alex: no, it's file-based; no outbound needed. forwarding happens only if you enable and point it to your internal aggregator.
[09:31] Priya: another perf note — KV caching interacts with batching in subtle ways: if you have heavy prefix reuse, batching can amplify cache hits; if not, batching amplifies cold reads. we can provide an instrumentation hook to estimate prefix reuse from traces.
[09:54] Jordan: what's the expected timeline from courier arrival to service up?
[09:58] Priya: smoke run + install typically 2-6 hours for a single node if drivers match, longer if kernel modules need build. for a small cluster maybe a day.
[10:08] Carmen: deployment orchestration — will you provide playbooks for kube and non-kube?
[10:14] Alex: yes, both. kube manifests and systemd-based runbooks. we'll include sample tolerations for GPU scheduling.
[10:23] Samir: can we lock down the node so runtime can't exfiltrate logs even accidentally? we need least privilege.
[10:30] Priya: runtime runs as a non-root user by default and we have a hardened mode with disabled outbound connectors. we'll include steps to enable strict RBAC.
[10:42] Jordan: switching gears — Priya, you mentioned kernel flags for quantized kernels. which ones are high impact?
[10:49] Priya: cpu affinity and NUMA balancing matter; for GPU we recommend disabling migratory balancing and enabling high-resolution timers. we'll list exact flags and container cgroup tweaks in the tuning doc.
[11:05] Tina: can you share the sample smoke-run output now?
[11:09] Alex: posted in the chat — artifact-delivery-checklist.pdf contains the smoke script and expected metrics.
[11:15] [11:15] Carmen: we saw a footnote about "KV prefetch bloom filters" in your doc — is that experimental?
[11:21] Priya: it's an optimization we've been testing; it reduces unnecessary disk reads during warmup. we'll mark it experimental and it's opt-in.
[11:29] Jordan: ok, final question — do you offer any swap policy if a driver/firmware mismatch causes regression during pilot?
[11:36] Alex: we have a rollback artifact and a hotfix channel for off-cycle patches; if it's a driver issue we coordinate with vendor and can supply a replacement bundle. contractual SLA terms apply.
[11:48] Priya: wrapping up — for pilot we propose: (1) ship artifact bundle Nov 10, (2) run smoke + perf Nov 11, (3) run 24-hour soak week of Nov 17, (4) evaluate metrics and tune quant/batching.
[12:05] Jordan: that timeline works. will confirm internal approvals.
[12:10] Alex: great. i'll shoot the checklist and SOW draft after the call.
[12:14] Carmen: one more ask — please include a minimal support contact for on-call during install.
[12:20] Alex: yes will include. thanks everyone.
[12:23] Tina: thanks.
[51:30] [end]
